title: Anthropic CFO Krishna Rao Holds Stake Calculated at About $703 Million Ahead of IPO
excerpt: Moneycontrol's calculations from Anthropic's IPO filing put CFO Krishna Rao's stake at about $703 million, or roughly Rs 6,500 crore. The filing itself lists Rao, 43, with 9,497,900 shares beneficially owned, mostly in stock options, the largest holding of any non-founder.
body:
• Anthropic CFO Krishna Rao holds a stake worth about $703 million (around Rs 6,500 crore), according to Moneycontrol's calculations based on the company's IPO filing.
  • The S-1 lists Rao with 9,497,900 shares beneficially owned, mostly stock options — the largest stake held by a non-founder.
  • Rao joined Anthropic in 2024 as its first CFO, after finance roles at Airbnb, where he helped raise more than $10 billion including its IPO, and as CFO of Fanatics Commerce.
  • Anthropic is reportedly seeking to raise around $90 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation in an IPO expected to launch next week, according to the Moneycontrol reporting cited by Inshorts.

Krishna Rao, the Indian-origin chief financial officer steering Anthropic toward the stock market, holds shares calculated to be worth about $703 million, according to Moneycontrol's calculations from the AI company's IPO filing, reported by Inshorts. In rupee terms the stake is about Rs 6,500 crore. The figure is a calculation from the filing, not a cash payout, and its final value depends on where the IPO prices.

Anthropic publicly filed its registration statement, Form S-1, with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on October 26, 2026, for a proposed offering of Class A common stock, and plans to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol ANT.

What the Filing Shows

The S-1's ownership table lists Rao, 43, with 9,497,900 shares beneficially owned as of September 30, 2026. Most of the holding is in stock options rather than shares held outright: a profile based on the filing puts his outright holding at 153,960 shares, with options on about 9.3 million more. Coverage of the filing notes he holds the largest stake of any non-founder, trailing only the seven co-founders, who each hold roughly 230 million to 245 million shares.

The filing also records his pay: total compensation of $720,250 in 2025, including a salary of $706,250. When he joined, he received options on 14 million shares at an exercise price of $1.30 each, vesting over four years, according to the filing coverage.

The Finance Chief Behind the Debut

Rao became Anthropic's first CFO in 2024. India Today describes him as responsible for the company's finances, fundraising and the major computing agreements that keep its Claude models running. Before Anthropic he was CFO of Fanatics Commerce and of Cedar, a healthcare payments startup. Earlier, at Airbnb, he worked on corporate and business development and helped the company raise more than $10 billion through equity and debt, including its December 2020 IPO. He began his career in consulting at Bain & Company and later worked in private equity at Blackstone.

That IPO experience is the reason his appointment drew attention: Anthropic hired a finance chief who had already taken a large technology company public before asking him to do it again.

The Offering Ahead

According to the Moneycontrol reporting, Anthropic is seeking to raise around $90 billion at a valuation of about $1.4 trillion, with the IPO expected to launch next week. Those figures are reported expectations, not terms set in the filing: the original S-1 left the number of shares and price range unset. An amended filing covered this week sets a price range of $70 to $78 a share, at which Rao's 9.5 million shares would be worth roughly $665 million to $741 million before option exercise costs — consistent with Moneycontrol's $703 million estimate.

Rao is one of four Indian-origin leaders named in coverage of Anthropic's IPO push, alongside chief technology officer Rahul Patil, Claude Code co-creator Sid Bidasaria and Neil "Buddy" Shah, who chairs the company's Long-Term Benefit Trust. For investors, though, Rao is the executive who will carry the numbers through the roadshow — and, on the filing's own figures, one of the offering's largest individual beneficiaries outside the founding group.
